'''Bank of Maharashtra''' (abbreviated as '''BoM''') is an Indian [[Public sector banks in India|public sector bank]], based in [[Pune]]. It was established in 1935 and [[Nationalization|nationalised]] by the [[Government of India]] in 1969. It has 2,641 branches, as of June 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Financial Results For Quarter Ended, 30th June 2025 |url=https://bankofmaharashtra.in/writereaddata/documentlibrary/0f76e3c6-256b-4306-bd61-3eae38ca1527.pdf |publisher=Bank of Maharashtra |access-date=15 August 2025}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Bank of Maharashtra , Bajirao Road.jpg|thumb|Bank of Maharashtra branch on Bajirao Road, a [[List of Grade III heritage structures in Pune|heritage structure in Pune]]]]
Bank of Maharashtra was established on 16 September 1935  in [[Poona]], [[Bombay Presidency]] (present day [[Pune]], [[Maharashtra]]), under the direction of [[Mahratta Chamber of Commerce, Industries and Agriculture|Mahratta Chamber of Commerce]] to assist small businesses and traders during the [[cooperative movement in India]].<ref name=":0"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Bank of Maharashtra: Rating reaffirmed; withdrawn for Rs. 600-crore Basel III tier II bonds |url=https://www.icra.in/Rationale/ShowRationaleReport?Id=136598 |publisher=ICRA |access-date=15 August 2025}}</ref>

BoM became a [[Scheduled Banks (India)|scheduled bank]] in 1944, obtained a [[banking license]] in 1955 under the [[Banking Regulation Act, 1949|Banking Companies Act]], and listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] in 1958.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Bank of Maharashtra - History and Growth |url=http://ir.unishivaji.ac.in:8080/jspui/bitstream/123456789/545/10/10_Chapter%204.pdf |publisher=Shivaji University |access-date=15 August 2025}}</ref>

In 1961, it acquired three smaller banks in Maharashtra, viz., Bank of Konkan in [[Malvan]], Bank of Nagpur in [[Nagpur]], and Bharat Industrial Bank in Poona.<ref>{{cite web |title=Banks which have closed down or amalgamated or placed under liquidation during the period 1st March to 4th September 1961 |url=https://www.rsdebate.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/556125/2/IQ_35_06091961_U447_p3402_p3404.pdf |publisher=Rajya Sabha Debates |access-date=15 August 2025}}</ref>

BoM was one of the [[Banking in India#Nationalisation in 1969|14 banks nationalised]] by the [[Government of India]] in July 1969.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bank of Maharashtra |url=https://www.acuite.in/documents/ratings/revised/28173-RR-20241218.pdf |publisher=Acuité Ratings & Research Limited |access-date=15 August 2025}}</ref>

In 1985, the bank opened its 500th Maharashtra branch at Nariman point, Mumbai, equiped with its first ALPM. Its Golden Jubilee year was inaugurated by RBI Governor Dr.Manmohan Singh.<ref name=":1" />

In 2004, BoM went public again with an [[initial public offering]], following which Government of India's ownership stake in the bank reduced from 100% to 76.77%.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bank of Maharashtra stock lists on BSE |url=https://zeenews.india.com/home/bank-of-maharashtra-stock-lists-on-bse_153919.html/amp |access-date=15 August 2025 |work=Zee News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Bank of Maharashtra |url=https://www.equitymaster.com/research-it/ipo/bom.asp |access-date=15 August 2025 |work=Equitymaster}}</ref>

In 2006, Bank of Maharashtra achieved a total business volume if ₹50,000 crore and launched its Core Banking Solution (CBS) implementation.<ref name=":1" />

In 2023, Bank of Maharashtra introduced "ARJUN" (Automated Remote Junction for Monitoring of Assets under Stress), A mobile application featuring an integrated dashboard for managing stressed assets.<ref name=":1" />

== Regional Rural Bank ==
BoM started three [[regional rural bank]]s (RRBs) in association with central and [[Government of Maharashtra|state governments]]: Marathwada Gramin Bank in [[Nanded]] (1976), Aurangabad-Jalna Gramin Bank in [[Aurangabad]] (1981), and Thane Gramin Bank in [[Thane]] (1986).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ray |first1=Partha |last2=Basu |first2=Sankarshan |title=Bank of Maharashtra: An Indian Small Public Sector Bank Unshackling itself from the baggage of the Past |url=https://www.nibmindia.org/documents/162/NIBM_Case_02_UsQmAix.pdf |publisher=National Institute of Bank Management |access-date=15 August 2025 |date=November 2022}}</ref> These RRBs were merged to create the [[Maharashtra Gramin Bank]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bank of Maharashtra merges two RRBs |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/bank-of-maharashtra-merges-two-rrbs/articleshow/2914903.cms |access-date=15 August 2025 |work=The Economic Times |date=31 March 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Maharashtra Gramin Bank |url=https://www.brickworkratings.com/Admin/PressRelease/Maharashtra-Gramin-Bank-23Dec2022%20(1).pdf |publisher=Brickwork Ratings |access-date=15 August 2025}}</ref> 

The [[Maharashtra Gramin Bank]] was further amalgamated on May 1, 2025 with Vidarbha Konkan Gramin Bank under The "One State, One RRB"<ref>{{cite web | author1=Livemint | title='One state-one RRB' to be effective from May 1 after govt approves consolidation of 15 regional rural banks | Mint | work=mint | date=8 April 2025 | url=https://www.livemint.com/economy/one-state-one-rrb-to-be-effective-from-may-1-after-govt-approves-consolidation-of-15-regional-rural-banks-11744118507326.html }}</ref> policy of [[Government of India]] to form single RRB per state. 

== Management ==

==== Board of Directors ====
As of 2026, the Bank of Maharashtra has Eight Board of Directors.<ref>https://bankofmaharashtra.bank.in/board-of-directors</ref>

* Shri Nidhu Saxena (Managing Director & Chief Excutive Officer)
* Shri Prabhat Kiran (Executive Director)
* Shri Sushanta Kumar Mohanty (Executive Director)
* Dr. Abhijit Phukon (Government Nominee Director)
* Shri Sanjeev Prakash (RBI Nominee Director)
* Shri Praveen Kumar (Shareholder Director)
* Shri Prasenjeet Shrikrishna Fadnavis (Shareholder Director)
